h: A cathedral city with plenty to explore
p: Peterborough is a city that surprises people. Just outside Queensgate, Cathedral Square is home to the old Guildhall, a pretty seventeenth-century building raised up on columns, and through the archway beyond stands the cathedral itself. Inside, look out for the grave of Katharine of Aragon, Henry VIII's first wife, who was buried here in 1536. Visitors still leave pomegranates, her emblem, beside her tomb.
Peterborough Museum, a short walk away on Priestgate, is a fun indoor stop with local history, Roman finds and a few spooky stories to tell, making it a handy rainy-day add-on for families.

If you fancy some fresh air, the Embankment along the River Nene is a pleasant walk close to the centre. A short drive out of town, Ferry Meadows in Nene Park is one of the area's big outdoor favourites, with lakes, walks, play areas and cycling. The Nene Valley Railway runs heritage steam and diesel trains on selected days, which is a cracking treat for railway fans young and old.

Combine a morning of shopping with an afternoon in the park and you've got a well-balanced day for all ages. Peterborough station is on the main line, with fast trains to London and the north, so it's an easy city to reach for a day without the car.
